title: The View from Above: Applications of Satellite Data in Economics
question: What can satellite data do for economics?
data: Survey of remote-sensing data and applications
main_finding: Introduces remote-sensing science and economic uses; no specific findings claimed beyond scope
how_my_project_differs: Applies the approach to collateral-level flood exposure and credit risk

authors: Tellman, B.; Sullivan, J.A.; Kuhn, C.; Kettner, A.J.; Doyle, C.S.; Brakenridge, G.R.; Erickson, T.A.; Slayback, D.A.; et al.
title: Satellite imaging reveals increased proportion of population exposed to floods
verified: verified 2026-11-02 via OpenAlex; preprint via Research Square
question: Where and how many people are exposed to observed floods; is the exposed share rising?
data: 12,719 MODIS images; DFO catalogue; GHSL population; Landsat validation points
identification: Descriptive measurement; accuracy assessment on 123 events
main_finding: 913 events mapped at 250 m; 2.23m km2 and 290m people affected; mean accuracy about 83%; urban, flash and cloud-covered floods often unmappable
how_my_project_differs: Uses GFD event 3850 as a 2011 exposure layer for Thai collateral, then links it to credit outcomes

authors: Pekel, J.-F.; Cottam, A.; Gorelick, N.; Belward, A.S.
title: High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes
question: Global surface water occurrence and change 1984-2021
main_finding: Not read (paper); dataset is 30 m monthly 1984-2021, free under Copernicus terms
how_my_project_differs: Candidate 30 m 2011 water layer to refine MODIS extent; not a flood product itself

authors: Kocornik-Mina, A.; McDermott, T.K.J.; Michaels, G.; Rauch, F.
title: Flooded Cities
verified: verified 2026-11-02 via OpenAlex; CEP DP 1398 PDF
question: Does economic activity move away from flood-prone urban areas?
data: DFO inundation maps (mainly 2003-08), night lights, elevation; 53 floods, 1,868 cities
identification: City-level flood indicator; within-city elevation contrasts; panel with fixed effects
main_finding: Low-elevation areas flood more yet hold more activity and recover as fast; little relocation; authors note DFO maps likely understate extent
how_my_project_differs: Collateral and credit outcomes rather than night lights; Thailand single-country with finer exposure

authors: Albertazzi, U.; Djekic, D.; Ponte Marques, A.
title: Physical climate risk, credit risk and lending activity
question: How do floods affect lending, rates, collateral and default?
data: AnaCredit; Copernicus EMS vector flood maps (Sentinel-1/2); Orbis; four European floods 2021-24
identification: Spatial RD at union of CEMS perimeters (300-500 m bandwidths); McCrary and balance tests; Khwaja-Mian FE
main_finding: Lending +3.5-5% in flood quarter then reverses; default +0.7 pp; demand dominates; main banks lend more but tighten collateral
how_my_project_differs: Emerging market with thin insurance and debt relief; collateral LGD and IFRS 9 staging; must handle SAR urban under-detection that CEMS manual mapping may partly avoid

authors: Noy, I.; Nguyen, C.; Patel, P.
title: Floods and Spillovers: Households after the 2011 Great Flood in Thailand
question: Direct and spillover effects of the 2011 Thai flood on households
data: Thai Household Socio-Economic Survey waves with 2012 flood module; satellite-based exposure indicators
identification: Self-reported and satellite exposure to separate direct and spillover households
main_finding: Estimates not read; analyses income, expenditure, assets, debt and savings
how_my_project_differs: Credit and collateral side rather than household welfare; but closest Thai precedent for satellite exposure

authors: Gandhi, S.; Kahn, M.E.; Kochhar, R.; Lall, S.; Tandel, V.
title: Adapting to Flood Risk: Evidence from a Panel of Global Cities
question: Are cities adapting to floods?
data: 3,931 major floods 2000-23; 9,468 cities; monthly night lights
identification: Panel event study on city night lights
main_finding: Night-light declines 3.5x larger in low-income countries; impacts falling over time; prior exposure reduces impacts

title: Geographic Boundaries as Regression Discontinuities
question: How to analyse RD designs at geographic boundaries
identification: Geographic RD as RD with two running variables
main_finding: Clarifies geography-specific issues; estimation and validation with pre-treatment covariates
how_my_project_differs: Applies GRD to flood edges where the boundary itself is measured with error

title: The Devil is in the Tails: Regression Discontinuity Design with Measurement Error in the Assignment Variable
question: Identification of RD when the assignment variable is mismeasured
identification: Sufficient conditions for identification with discrete/continuous mismeasured running variable
main_finding: First-stage discontinuity may vanish under measurement error; identification restored under stated conditions
how_my_project_differs: Relevant to distance-to-flood-edge measured from noisy satellite perimeters

title: Regression discontinuity design with continuous measurement error in the running variable
question: RD with continuous measurement error in the running variable
identification: Nonparametric estimator under non-differential error with auxiliary sample
main_finding: Identification fails with continuous error; consistent LATE estimator with auxiliary data
how_my_project_differs: Auxiliary validation (e.g. official Thai extents) could play the role of their auxiliary sample

authors: Sampson, C.C.; Smith, A.M.; Bates, P.D.; Neal, J.C.; Alfieri, L.; Freer, J.E.
title: A high-resolution global flood hazard model
question: Can a global flood hazard model be built and validated?
data: Global terrain and hydrology; UK and Canada benchmark maps
main_finding: About 90 m return-period maps; captures two-thirds to three-quarters of benchmark at-risk area; MAE about 5% at 1 km
how_my_project_differs: Hazard (ex-ante) layer for pricing tests, distinct from realised satellite extents

authors: Trigg, M.A.; Birch, C.E.; Neal, J.C.; Bates, P.D.; Smith, A.; Sampson, C.C.; Yamazaki, D.; Hirabayashi, Y.; Pappenberger, F.; Dutra, E.; et al.
title: The credibility challenge for global fluvial flood risk analysis
verified: verified 2026-11-02 via Crossref; IOP open-access PDF
question: How consistent are global flood hazard models?
data: Six global models compared for Africa
main_finding: About 30-40% agreement in flood extent; large differences in deltas, arid zones, wetlands; limited validation against observed floods
how_my_project_differs: Motivates validating any hazard map against realised Thai extents before using it as ex-ante risk

authors: Rentschler, J.; Salhab, M.; Jafino, B.A.
title: Flood exposure and poverty in 188 countries
question: How many people face high flood risk and poverty?
data: Global poverty and flood hazard data (source not identified in abstract)
main_finding: 1.81bn people exposed to 1-in-100-year floods; 89% in low- and middle-income countries
how_my_project_differs: Uses hazard maps for credit exposure rather than poverty

authors: Chini, M.; Pelich, R.; Pulvirenti, L.; Pierdicca, N.; Hostache, R.; Matgen, P.
title: Sentinel-1 InSAR Coherence to Detect Floodwater in Urban Areas: Houston and Hurricane Harvey as A Test Case
question: Can Sentinel-1 detect floodwater in urban areas?
data: Sentinel-1 StripMap and IW (5 m and 20 m); VHR optical, crowdsourced points, FEMA model
identification: Building detection plus InSAR coherence change
main_finding: Algorithm detects urban floodwater in Houston; evaluated qualitatively against independent data
how_my_project_differs: Possible route to reduce urban under-detection for post-2015 Thai floods

authors: DeVries, B.; Huang, C.; Armston, J.; Huang, W.; Jones, J.W.; Lang, M.W.
title: Rapid and robust monitoring of flood events using Sentinel-1 and Landsat data on the Google Earth Engine
question: Rapid flood mapping with open SAR on GEE
data: All Sentinel-1 images plus historical Landsat water probabilities
main_finding: Area-normalised accuracy 89.8 +/- 2.8% for Houston; 1.6-9.8 pp better than simple threshold
how_my_project_differs: Reproducible open pipeline candidate for Thai post-2015 events

authors: Komori, D.; Nakamura, S.; Kiguchi, M.; Nishijima, A.; Yamazaki, D.; Suzuki, S.; Kawasaki, A.; Oki, K.; Oki, T.
title: Characteristics of the 2011 Chao Phraya River flood in Central Thailand
question: What were the hydrological characteristics of the 2011 flood?
data: Rainfall, dam and discharge records; Thai government damage figures
main_finding: 813 dead; flood volume about 15bn m3; damaged agricultural land peaked at 18,291 km2 (14 Nov 2011); 7 industrial estates and 804 companies inundated
how_my_project_differs: Benchmark for validating any satellite 2011 extent

title: Global Flood Monitoring (GFM) - Product User Manual
venue: Copernicus EMS / JRC technical report (GFM Deliverable 5.2)
question: What does the operational Sentinel-1 flood product deliver and where does it fail?
main_finding: 20 m; archive from 1 Jan 2015; excludes urban and dense vegetation as no-sensitivity areas; no-sensitivity leads mostly to under-estimation
how_my_project_differs: Primary open source for post-2015 Thai flood extents; its exclusion mask defines where collateral exposure is unobservable
